description.narrative:
Mekong Regional Water Governance Program (PMU) supports Department of Water Resource (DWR) in Laos through Oxfam in Laos office while the budget is covered from PMU, however the partnership management is still under Laos office focal point of Inclusion Project 2 (IP2).
Background: The reference on the Dublin principles is 1. Freshwater is a finite and vulnerable resource, essential to sustain life, development and the environment; 2. Water development and management should be based on a participatory approach, involving users, planners, and policymakers at all levels; 3. Women play a central part in the provision, management and safeguarding of waterand, 4. Water has an economic value in all its competing uses and should be recognized as an economic good.
Since 2018, the Laos Department of Water Resources was prepared on draft the National Water and Water Resources Strategy that there are 10 strategies and there is identify on the role of gender into implementation action plan, but this strategy is not yet identified on strategy and action plan on gender mainstream on water resources. The reference meeting on 1-3 July 2020 at VangVieng District, Vientiane Province that identified on objectives, Goal, Work plan etc. Moreover, the reference meetingon 27 November 2020 at Thalat, Vientiane Province and 18 December 2020 at Paksan District, Bolikhamxay Province on consultation with line agencies on draft gender mainstream for IWRMplan. However, this draft planning is need proposed and consultation with water sector at local area to exchange idea to it.
The support will focus:
Activity 01: Consultation meeting on the road map on gender mainstream on Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) which will invitational water agencies at the centrallevel and the water sector at province levels. There are shared ideas and action plans of water governance for the link to gender in water development sectors.
Activity 02: Analysis and the draft of the road map on gender mainstream on IWRM. There are reviews on the water plans of water governments and the water sector in provincesand identify priorities on gender mainstream on IWRM. Moreover, it will expend on mechanism, monitoring, and evaluation of the implementation of this road map.

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam has had a presence in Lao PDR for longer than most INGOs, with both Oxfam in Belgium (OBE) and Oxfam Australia (OAU) beginning programming and establishing offices in the late 1980s. Oxfam’s vision is of a Laos in which all citizens – particularlywomen, the marginalised and discriminated groups – are able to claim their right to access opportunities and resources so as to overcome all forms of poverty and injustice.
Since 2015, the work of Oxfam in the country is governed by the Oxfam Country Strategy (2015-2019).We seek transformative changes in policies, practices and beliefs in ways that fundamentally improve the lives of poor and marginalised women and men, and ensure that all citizens have the same opportunities to enjoy their rights. Todo so, Oxfam focuses its work on four Domains of Change: Citizen Participation and Civil Society Development, Gender Justice, Resilient Communities and Sustainable Development, and Responsible Investment.
For this project, Oxfam in Laos will support theexpansion of the influencing work and public campaign on advocating for more inclusive social protection and access to social protection of the most marginalized workers. National public events will be organised, such Eliminate Violence Against Women Day(EVAW), and digital platforms will be used to socialize the information, and stir discussion and dialogue among rights holders, government stakeholders and policy makers. The campaigns will be implemented nationwide and in the provinces where Oxfam in Laos works. Target groups include marginalized workers, youth,women, CSOs as well as government stakeholders.
